chapter: Suntaug Lake Inn and Duke Ellington's band
title: The Mingus and Tizol fight at the Apollo
summary: They recall Mingus, Tizol and the fire axe, Duke not firing people, and Mingus turning a table over at Earl Hines's club.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Did you know Barney very well.

I didn't know him very well but he and Tizol, they were two guys that left early, see. But Tizol -- Charlie Mingus, remember when Charlie Mingus was with the band. He died here recently and Charlie was with the band and he and Tricky -- I mean, what's the name the trombone player, Tizol, they couldn't get along.
They had that big fight at the Apollo Theatre. Were you there that time.
Yeah, I was there.
How did that thing go.
I told Duke you better get one of them off because Tizol is going to cut them down. That was awful. But I told Duke, Mingus' fault, Mingus was a agitator.
Go on and tell it. How did it happen.

I wasn't there when it started but I know they were agitating, see and Tizol was one, you were supposed -- like a director, see. Now they play it this way, because he copied the music and knew how it went. And Mingus and them got to arguing about something and I called Duke, I said, man Tizol is going to cut him down because Tizol was
really going to cut them I think.
Mingus had the fire axe or something, didn't he. Didn't Mingus have the fire axe after Tizol.
Oh, I don't know what they did. Anyway
It's in the record that perhaps the only person that Duke really ever fired was Mingus because he just hated to fire anybody. He would find some reason to get them out.
He didn't fire anybody.
But he told Mingus he thought he better go. That they couldn't get along. I remember reading that some place.

Well, I was down to a place where Earl Hines was playing and Mingus was on the side and Mingus got up to play and he was playing and you know, how parties sit down and start talking and Mingus took his horn and turned the table over.
His bass fiddle, you mean.
Yeah, his fiddle and turned the table over. And I had to go and get Earl back on the stage again. This was down at some club, nightclub.
Go on and talk, Tom.
That ended. Mingus was relieved. But they used to say Mingus was a great bass player. They used to tell me that Mingus was a great bass player, but --
I believe so, I really do.
Yeah.
Yes.
Well, I couldn't see it.

I think Mingus like, and this is in my humble opinion, Tom, of course, I'm not supposed to be talking but in my humble opinion I use him like Duke, he was so far ahead of the time and you know Duke was ahead of time, I think people are going to in the next few years, begin to recognize what a great person he was. It was like Duke's music was a little bit ahead of time.
But that's my humble opinion because I'm a bass player and I think perhaps I'm prejudiced.
